title: Who's Who: Amara Quill
summary: Experimental philosopher whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Amara Quill (1802–1871) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a experimental philosopher whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Quill designed the shaped interruptions that demonstrated an aperture could be addressed and could answer. A rigorous skeptic of easy claims about intelligence in the Stratum, she maintained that a reply need not have a speaker.
Her distinction still guides the interpretation of apparently meaningful sonances.

For Alderwick readers, Amara Quill is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
